elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with neck pain and any of:
elements.text: Neck stiffness and any of: temperature ≥ 38°C, headache, drowsy/confused or purple/red rash: meningitis likely. Give ceftriaxone 2g IV1/IM. Avoid injecting > 1g IM at one injection site

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with neck pain and any of:
elements.text: Neurological symptoms in arms/legs: weakness, numbness, clumsiness, stiffness, change in gait or difficulty with co-ordination

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with neck pain and any of:
elements.text: Recent injury and x-ray unavailable/abnormal or neurological symptoms: apply rigid neck collar and immobilise head with tape and sandbags/IV fluid bags on either side of head

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with neck pain and any of:
elements.text: Refer urgently.

Wrist/hand pain: intermittent, worse at night, relieved by shaking. May be numbness/tingling in 1st, 2nd and 3rd fingers or weakness of hand.

Carpal tunnel syndrome likely • Give ibuprofen2 400mg 8 hourly with/after food and paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Splint wrist in neutral position at night. • Refer to occupational therapist.
If no better after 6 weeks or worsens, refer to doctor.
Elbow pain with or after elbow flexion/extension.
May have decreased grip strength.
Tennis or golfer’s elbow likely • Apply ice to elbow and rest arm. • Give ibuprofen2 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for 10 days. • Refer for physiotherapy.
Thumb pain: worse with thumb/wrist movement or catching/locking of finger.
Tenosynovitis likely • Rest and splint joint. • Give ibuprofen2 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for up to 5 days. • Refer to occupational therapist.
Approach to the patient with arm or hand symptoms not needing urgent attention

• Check joints and ask patient to place hands behind head, then behind back. Bury nails in palm to make a fist and open hand. Press palms together with elbows lifted. • If joint warm/tender/swollen or unable to do all actions comfortably, joint problem likely 77.

1Do not mix Ringer's lactate and IV ceftriaxone. 2Avoid if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease, pregnant. If patient also taking aspirin, advise to wait at least 30 minutes after taking aspirin before taking ibuprofen.

Approach to the patient with neck pain not needing urgent attention Any of: >50 years, pain progressive or lasting > 6 weeks, oral steroid use, HIV, diabetes, IV drug use, unexplained weight loss/fever or TB, neck surgery, previous cancer?
Yes • Do cervical spine x-ray. • Refer to doctor.

No • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) for up to 5 days. If no response, give ibuprofen2 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for up to 5 days. • If no better after 5 days and no arm pain, refer for physiotherapy. If pain ≥ 3 months, assess and advise 76. • If no better after 6 weeks, arm pain, weakness/numbness develops or pain worsens, do cervical spine x-rays and refer.
